results.text: Linel's pictures are a sort of, up guards on Adam paintings, and Mason's exquisite idles are as national as a jingo poem. Mister Berkett Foster's landscapes smile at one much in the same way that Mister Carker used to flash his teeth. And Mister John Collier gives his sitter a cheerful slap on the back before he says, "Like a shampooer in a Turkish bath, next man."
